about.description: Hand labels for 10 of the 20 synthetic transcripts (2 per rep). Turn numbers are 1-based and refer to data/transcripts/<id>.txt.
about.rubric: Same rubric the analysis prompt uses (fieldcoach/prompts/analysis.md): discovery questions are labeled per rep turn; each objection once, at the customer turn where it first comes up; handling judged on everything the rep says in response.

labels.discovery_turns: rep turns that contain at least one discovery question
labels.objections: customer turn, category, handling (strong | adequate | weak | unaddressed)

about.caveat: Labels were written together with the synthetic transcripts by a single annotator. Treat the numbers as a regression signal, not a benchmark.

T01.notes: Turns 15 and 21 end with checks ('Would afternoon-only testing work for you?', 'Does that change the picture?'), not discovery. Both objections get acknowledge, clarify, specifics and a check.

T03.notes: Turn 13 answers the liability concern with specifics but no acknowledgment, question or check, so adequate. The failed cholesterol program (turns 6-8) is history, not an objection.

T05.notes: Turn 2 ('heard a lot of pitches') has no concrete concern. Turn 8 states buying criteria before any pitch, so not an objection.

T07.notes: Turn 17 gives specifics and a check but no acknowledgment or clarifying question, so adequate.

T09.notes: Turn 1 is small talk. Turn 12 ('What's the minimum order?') is a neutral question. Turn 14 is about losing a wholesaler rebate, so cost_margin.

T11.notes: Turn 12 repeats the swabbing concern, so it is not a new objection. 'After the holidays, maybe' has no firm time.

T13.notes: Turn 10 brings staffing back up; same concern as turn 2, not listed again.

T15.notes: Turn 10 ('What happens if it breaks?') is a worry about equipment, so other. Turn 12 ('not ready to commit') gives no reason.

T17.notes: Turn 9 changes the subject to window signage, so the liability concern is unaddressed. 'My email's on the back' is not a next step.

T19.notes: Turn 7 ignores the CLIA worry and talks about kit price. Turn 12 is a brush-off without a new concern.
